See also: Popa, pöpa, popã, and popă

Asturian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Vulgar Latin *puppa, from Latin puppis (“stern”), possibly with influence from prora (“prow”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpopa/ [ˈpo.pa]
  • Rhymes: -opa
  • Syllabification: po‧pa

Noun

[edit]

popa f (plural popes)

  1. stern, poop
    Synonym: proba

Further reading

[edit]
  • Xosé Lluis García Arias (2002–2004), “popa”, in Diccionario general de la lengua asturiana [General Dictionary of the Asturian Language] (in Spanish), Editorial Prensa Asturiana, →ISBN
  • “popa”, in Diccionariu de la llingua asturiana [Dictionary of the Asturian Language] (in Asturian), 1st edition, Academy of the Asturian Language [Asturian: Academia de la Llingua Asturiana], 2000, →ISBN

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Vulgar Latin *puppa, from Latin puppis (“stern”), possibly with influence from prora (“prow”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [ˈpo.pə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ˈpo.pa]

Noun

[edit]

popa f (plural popes)

  1. stern, poop
    Antonym: proa
    • 2002, Albert Sánchez Piñol, chapter 1, in La pell freda, La Campana, →ISBN:
      Feia trenta-tres dies que els dofins havien renunciat a la nostra popa i dinou que la tripulació expel·lia núvols de baf per la boca.
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)
Derived terms
[edit]
  • anar en popa
  • anar vent en popa
  • de popa a proa
  • empopar
  • poper

Etymology 2

[edit]

Inherited from Latin puppa, variant of pūpa (“girl”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [ˈpo.pə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ˈpo.pa]

Noun

[edit]

popa f (plural popes)

  1. (colloquial, Lleida) boob, titty

Etymology 3

[edit]

Borrowed from Romanian popa and/or Russian поп (pop).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [ˈpɔ.pə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ˈpo.pa]

Noun

[edit]

popa m (plural popes)

  1. (Eastern Orthodoxy) pope (any Russian Orthodox priest)

References

[edit]
  • “popa” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.
  • “popa”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026
  • “popa”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007

Fala

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpopa/
  • Rhymes: -opa
  • Syllabification: po‧pa

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Latin upupa.

Noun

[edit]

popa f (plural popas)

  1. (Valverdeñu) a hoopoe, especially a Eurasian hoopoe
    Synonyms: galu de campu (Lagarteiru, Valverdeñu), abubilla (Mañegu, Valverdeñu)

Etymology 2

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese popa, from Vulgar Latin *puppa.

Noun

[edit]

popa f (plural popas)

  1. stern, poop

References

[edit]
  • Valeš, Miroslav (2021), Diccionariu de A Fala: lagarteiru, mañegu, valverdeñu (web)‎[1], 2nd edition, Minde, Portugal: CIDLeS, published 2022, →ISBN, page 230

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Homophones: popas, popât

Verb

popa

  1. third-person singular past historic of poper

  • Hyphenation: po‧pa

Noun

Spanish

Inherited from Old Spanish popa, from Vulgar Latin *puppa, from Latin puppis (“stern”), possibly with influence from prora (“prow”).

Pronunciation

  • IPA(key): /ˈpopa/ [ˈpo.pa]
  • Rhymes: -opa
  • Syllabification: po‧pa

Noun

[edit]

popa f (plural popas)

  1. stern, poop (back of a boat or ship)
    Antonym: proa

Derived terms

[edit]

  • de popa a proa
  • viento en popa
